newsitem.title: UK: Millwall to announce restructuring deal.
newsitem.headline: Millwall to announce restructuring deal.

text.p: Millwall Holdings, the parent of London soccer club Millwall, will announce a 10 million stg corporate restructuring on Friday led by Greek-Cypriot businessman Theo Paphitis, the Financial Times said.
The club will be part of a larger company focusing on hosting sporting and entertainment events at its south London stadium.
And according to the report, the money will be raised through a 6.4 million stg placing and a 3.6 million stg equity issue.
Existing shareholders will be offered shares in the new company which may be called New London Stadium via a two-for-one rights issue at 1p a share.

Millwall was floated on the stock market in 1989 at 20p a share but the shares were suspended in January this year at 4p after the management called in administrators when the club was unable to pay interest on its 10 million stg debts without having to sell players.

After the reconstruction the club will have three million stg in cash and be capitalised at just under 12 million stg. The money raised in the refinancing will be used to pay off existing debts on the stadium and to repay bank loans.
Trading in the shares is expected to resume in June, the newspaper report said.
Paphitis will take over as executive chairman from Peter Mead who will become vice chairman. The deal was put together by the administrators Buchler Phillips and brokers Townsley & Co.
